pages.title: Database relationships & ownership
pages.status: REVIEW DRAFT / 28 OCT 2026 / No live database changes

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: For the KodeHub and analytics builders to agree which records are shared, which application changes them, and how to avoid another Tracker-versus-OClass split. An ERD shows relationships; the ownership matrix assigns responsibility.

sections.title: Two models, clearly separated
sections.body: CURRENT pages describe the local schema.sql at commit 65c0a85 (38 application tables). PROPOSED pages reflect the academy-wide workflow confirmed on 28 October. They are discussion designs, not implemented tables or approved migration SQL. The colleague's migrated schema has not been supplied.

sections.title: Main design correction
sections.body: Students in the same class/time slot may study completely different modules and lessons. A student-module record must own learning progress independently of a class timetable. Moving a student must preserve their module, documentation, assignments and reports.

sections.title: How to read this document
sections.body: Blue boxes show existing concepts; green boxes show proposed concepts. PK identifies a row; FK links it to another row. 1:N means one parent may have zero or many children. Diagrams show selected keys and relationships; the inventory lists all 38 existing tables. Editable schema-reference files contain their CREATE and later ALTER statements.

sections.title: Evidence and scope
sections.body: Sources: schema.sql and forward migrations, PRODUCTION-PARITY.md, route guards, confirmed product discussion, and the three-page teacher checklist supplied by Gio. No student records, credentials or payment data are included. Local schema existence does not establish deployment or live verification.

pages.title: Current: classes and attendance
notes: Class membership, dated weekly-slot membership and attendance are separate records. They must not be treated as interchangeable. The supplied checklist also requires expected absences and make-up students.

Gap: classes has no dedicated class-code column, and weekly slots have a start time but no end time/duration. The requested timetable needs stable class-code mapping, duration and center time-zone rules. Source: schema.sql:43-93, 2246-2263.

pages.title: Current: curriculum and assignments
pages.status: CURRENT LOCAL SCHEMA / Class-level course assignment

nodes.name: class_course_assignments
fields: At most one active course per class

notes: Existing class-course history permits one active course per class. Individual completion records do not solve the requirement for different active modules within the same time slot.

Assignments also reference that class-course link. A future learner-module design must update assignment targeting as well as Journey display; preserve published assignment snapshots, submissions and reviews. Source: schema.sql:993-1348 and 1980-1986.

pages.title: Current: submissions and publications
pages.status: CURRENT LOCAL SCHEMA / History and family visibility

nodes.name: student_feedback
fields: PK id; FK student, class, lesson

nodes.name: published_feedback
fields: PK id; FK feedback_id + scope keys

notes: Families read their child's permitted submissions and non-withdrawn publications. Private drafts are separate. Existing report publication is one snapshot per report row; a new exported report is required for a new version.

Current student_media is student-linked private Storage metadata; session_videos stores Drive links. Neither is the complete proposed student + session + module + lesson documentation model. Module criterion grades and awards are not yet modeled. Source: schema.sql:684, 1516-1553, 1776-1817, 2350.

pages.title: Current: credits and retry records
pages.status: CURRENT LOCAL SCHEMA / Credits are session units, not money

nodes.name: financial payment records
fields: Do not send finance data to families

notes: Attendance charges/refunds and account changes commit through authorized RPCs. A receipt makes an exact repeated request return its prior result. Not every older endpoint or roster operation has this protection.

Current credit_accounts contains no center_id; scope is derived through the student. The shared design must choose one ledger owner. Finance may grant credit units, while KodeHub consumes/refunds them; neither app should maintain an independent editable balance. Source: schema.sql:764-795.

pages.title: Proposed: learning belongs to students
pages.status: PROPOSED / Names and migration mapping require joint review

nodes.name: STUDENT_MODULE
fields: A repeat module is a new attempt

nodes.name: LEARNING_ACTIVITY
fields: Several activities may occur per class

nodes.name: DOCUMENTATION / MEDIA
fields: Media: Drive file ID + media type

notes: A class groups students by schedule; each learner has independent module attempts. Each activity links one student's dated session to the module/lesson actually studied. Validate that progress, activity and lesson all refer to the same module and student.

Source mapping is not a migration plan: classes/enrollments/slots remain scheduling concepts; courses/course_lessons are candidates for modules/lessons. Existing class lessons, progress and IDs must be reconciled before conversion. Drive stays academy-controlled; private parent playback remains a release test.

pages.title: Proposed: checklist supervision
pages.status: PROPOSED / Based on supplied 3-page checklist; scope assignments are recommendations
notes: 38 checkboxes: Pre-class 7; Before class 4; Opening 5; Delivery 8; Breaktime 3; End of class 5; Parent communication 3; Admin duties 3. Page 3 gives guidance, not extra scored tasks. The PDF does not assign database scope; proposed class/student splits need review.

Overview = completed applicable results / all applicable results for the selected sessions. Count class items once and student items per applicable learner. Show pending separately from overdue; future stages are not yet due. N/A needs a reason; no applicable tasks shows N/A, not 100%.

pages.title: Proposed: reports and grade legend
pages.status: PROPOSED / Report page confirmed; grade descriptions proposed
rows: Competition-level mastery: exceptional skill and independence in competition-level challenges; teacher assessment, not an external certification.
Advanced achievement: consistently exceeds module expectations with confident, independent work.
Strong achievement: meets module expectations confidently and independently.
Developing confidence: meets most expectations with occasional guidance.
Steady progress: demonstrates growing understanding with some guidance.
Developing understanding: builds skills through regular guidance and practice.
Building foundations: develops essential skills with close guidance.
pages.notes: Dedicated Module Reports page: select student and module attempt, enter five criterion grades, write feedback, preview, publish and export PDF. Criteria: coding, building/designing, creativity, problem solving, communication. Include Kodecoon logo, student/module name and legend. Store report -> student_module, report -> criterion grades, and immutable publication -> report revision. Snapshot criterion wording, grade meaning and displayed names. Recommend 'Not assessed' when not observed; not a low grade.

pages.title: Proposed: responsibility for data changes
pages.status: PROPOSED / No assumption that the colleague's migrated database accepts writes
rows: Shared core agreed with colleague. Reuse canonical IDs. KodeHub changes use the agreed API or controlled database operation.
KodeHub: permitted operational fields. Analytics: approved fields/views.
One shared record; staff changes through KodeHub after ownership agreement. Do not maintain a second editable roster.
Both apps read the same effective-dated history.
KodeHub owns modules, learner progress, Drive references, module reports and award albums. Awards need a new student-linked record plus media links.
Parents: only their child's shared records. Analytics: permitted summaries.
KodeHub owns versioned template, results, completion history and supervisor review.
Staff-only; analytics receives completion aggregates if approved.
One shared ledger. Finance grants units using an external operation ID; KodeHub records usage/refunds and authorized adjustments.
Balance and unit history only. No payment amount or banking details.
Finance domain maintained outside KodeHub access. Final owner to be agreed with colleague.
Analytics access only as authorized. KodeHub and parent APIs receive no financial rows.
pages.notes: An ERD documents relationships; this matrix assigns responsibility. 'Shared' means one canonical record, not necessarily one physical database. Different databases can integrate through controlled APIs. Analytics should not independently rewrite operational records. No credentials or live records are needed for this comparison.

pages.title: Integration, permissions and handoff
pages.status: PROPOSED / Decisions to settle with the analytics builder

sections.title: Use the migration already completed
sections.body: First inspect her table/column list, keys, duplicate-resolution rules and update process. Is it a database used for daily edits or a periodically refreshed analytics copy? Preserve canonical IDs; map legacy Tracker/OClass identifiers through a source-ID mapping. Never join students by name alone.

sections.title: One balance and an explicit cutover
sections.body: Reconcile student identity, active enrolments and opening credit units before rollout. Each imported operation needs a stable external ID to reject duplicate delivery. Stop editing the old tracker for the records transferred to the agreed system. Do not synchronize two independently editable balances.

sections.title: Safe staff and family access
sections.body: Teacher and center manager have equal staff permissions per the confirmed product direction; current guards still accept teacher/admin. Enforce role, academy and child scope in pages, APIs and database policies. Parent URLs never authorize access by themselves. Parents see only linked children and shared work; no supervisor checklist, draft staff notes or finance access.

sections.title: Assignments must follow individual learning too
sections.body: Existing assignment_learners, submission versions and reviews can be preserved. Proposed assignment targets must reference the learner's module attempt, with an optional class/session context. Validate lesson/module consistency. Publishing captures the brief and recipients; changing a time slot does not erase submissions or reviews.

sections.title: What to exchange next
sections.body: Share this PDF and the editable schema index. Ask for her ERD/schema, canonical student and class identifiers, imported-field list, update ownership and synchronization approach. Compare before writing migrations. Confirm where staff adds new students and where new credit grants originate.

sections.title: No deployment claim
sections.body: Existing RLS and migration test sources exist, but none were run for this document. The PDF was checked for legibility and coverage. Drive parent playback, multi-center authorization, data reconciliation and live integration remain implementation/release work.
